attribution.note: Marcus's own sentence in his own Substack post. He is not quoting anyone; the colon introduces his supporting material.

semantics.note: The proposition keeps 'thus far', the hype/ROI contrast and the comparison with gen AI. 'Looks to be' is a mild hedge on an observation, not a probabilistic forecast, so the claim can still be scored.

contract.note: Reading 'not so much ROI' as 'only a minority report significant or clear returns' is an ordinary, fair reading. The result depends on that threshold: surveys asking about looser 'measurable value' give majority figures.

evidence.note: Large survey, fieldwork Dec 2025 to Jan 2026, released before the post. Only 23% of leaders report significant ROI from agents. It comes from a vendor that sells agents, which if anything argues against bias toward this finding.
June 2025 Reuters report of Gartner's analysis: most agentic offerings lack significant value or ROI, and most projects are driven by hype. Supports both halves of the claim.

May 2025 PwC survey: 66% of adopters report measurable productivity value. This counts against the claim only under a looser threshold than 'significant ROI', and PwC itself says the gains stop short of transformation.
Secondary summary of a vendor study. Its 88% positive-ROI figure covers 'early adopters' only, and coverage disputes whether it is agent-specific. Context only.

reviews.rationale: On the contract's plain reading (only a minority report significant returns), e1 (23% significant agent ROI, early 2026) and e2 (Gartner: most agentic offerings lack significant value; hype-driven) support the claim. e3's 66% figure measures looser self-reported productivity value, not significant ROI, so it qualifies the claim without overturning it.
